This meant that a British subject who had spent most of his life in Australia could be deported. Re Canavan 2017 263 CLR 284 considered the disqualification of various members of Parliament for owing allegiance to a foreign power. One of those was Nick Xenophon, who held British Overseas Citizenship (BOC) due to being born in Cyprus while it was a British possession. The court held that because BOC did not grant a right of abode in the UK, it could not be considered citizenship, despite its name. This sparked the case of Newman v Minister for Health and Aged Care (2021) FCA 517, where Mr Newman wanted to argue that there was a Constitutional right of return; however, due to the short length of the ban, the court only heard and decided matters of administrative law, which Mr Newman lost.
